http.label: HTTP(s)
http.description: UP when the response status is accepted.

keyword.label: HTTP(s) - Keyword
keyword.description: UP when the response body contains (or lacks) a keyword.

json-query.label: HTTP(s) - Json Query
json-query.description: UP when a JSONata expression over the JSON response matches.

real-browser.label: HTTP(s) - Browser Engine (Chrome/Chromium)
real-browser.description: Loads the page in a real Chromium through a remote Playwright browser; UP on a 2xx/3xx navigation.

port.label: TCP Port
port.description: UP when a TCP connection succeeds.

ping.label: Ping
ping.description: UP when the host answers ICMP echo requests.

dns.label: DNS
dns.description: UP when the resolver returns a record.

docker.label: Docker Container
docker.description: UP when the container is running (and healthy, if it has a health check).

push.label: Push
push.description: Your system calls a URL on a schedule; silence means DOWN.

manual.label: Manual
manual.description: Status set by hand, never checked.

group.label: Group
group.description: Aggregates child monitors: DOWN when any child is down.

grpc-keyword.label: gRPC(s) - Keyword
grpc-keyword.description: Calls a unary gRPC method and looks for a keyword in the response.

websocket-upgrade.label: WebSocket Upgrade
websocket-upgrade.description: Opens a WebSocket and judges the close code (default 1000).

mqtt.label: MQTT
mqtt.description: Subscribes to a topic and checks the first message received.

kafka-producer.label: Kafka Producer
kafka-producer.description: Produces a message to a topic; UP when the brokers acknowledge it.

rabbitmq.label: RabbitMQ
rabbitmq.description: Queries the management API health check of each node.

smtp.label: SMTP
smtp.description: Connects to a mail server and verifies the handshake.

snmp.label: SNMP
snmp.description: Reads an OID over SNMP v1/v2c and optionally compares its value.

ntp.label: NTP
ntp.description: Queries a time server and checks stratum, offset and dispersion.

sftp.label: SFTP
sftp.description: Logs in over SFTP and optionally checks that a path exists.

radius.label: Radius
radius.description: Sends an Access-Request; UP unless the server rejects it.

tailscale-ping.label: Tailscale Ping
tailscale-ping.description: Runs `tailscale ping` on the worker host.

mysql.label: MySQL/MariaDB
mysql.description: Connects and runs a query (default SELECT 1).

postgres.label: PostgreSQL
postgres.description: Connects and runs a query (default SELECT 1).

sqlserver.label: Microsoft SQL Server
sqlserver.description: Connects and runs a query (default SELECT 1).

mongodb.label: MongoDB
mongodb.description: Connects and runs a command (default ping), optionally checking the result.

steam.label: Steam Game Server
steam.description: Looks the server up in the Steam master list (needs a Steam API key).

gamedig.label: GameDig
gamedig.description: Queries a game server with the GameDig protocol library.

statusCodes.label: Accepted status codes
statusCodes.description: Codes or ranges counted as UP, e.g. 200-299, 304.

tags.label: Tags
tags.empty: No tags yet. <link>Create tags</link> to label monitors.
tags.description: Shown in the monitor list and on status pages that enable tags. <link>Manage tags</link>

general.title: General
general.description: What to watch and how it shows up in the list.
general.name: Friendly name
general.invertKeywordDescription: UP when the keyword is absent.
general.jsonQueryDescription: JSONata expression evaluated against the result, e.g. data[0].ok.
general.manualStatusDescription: Manual monitors are never checked; they show the status you set.
general.dockerHostEmpty: No Docker hosts yet; an admin can add one in <link>settings</link>.
general.push: A push URL is generated when the monitor is saved. Call it at least every interval; a missed call marks the monitor DOWN.
general.groupEmpty: Create a Group monitor to nest monitors under it.
general.groupDescription: Groups aggregate the status of their children.
general.descriptionPlaceholder: Shown on the detail page and status pages.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: How often to check and how patient to be before alerting.
timing.retriesDescription: Failed checks before the monitor is marked DOWN.
timing.resendDescription: Every N consecutive DOWN beats (0 = never)

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: How to reach the service and what to ask it.
connection.connectionStringDescription: Credentials are stored with the monitor; use a read-only account.
connection.commandDescription: JSON command document run against the database (default {example}).
connection.redisIgnoreTlsDescription: Accept self-signed certificates on rediss:// connections.
connection.successMessageDescription: The received message must contain this text (leave empty to accept any message).
connection.brokersDescription: Bootstrap broker addresses, one per line.
connection.enableSslDescription: Connect to the brokers over TLS.
connection.autoTopicDescription: Create the topic when it does not exist.
connection.saslOptionsDescription: JSON object: mechanism (plain, scram-sha-256, scram-sha-512), username, password. Leave empty for no authentication.
connection.methodDescription: lowerCamelCase method name of the service.
connection.enableTlsDescription: Use TLS credentials for the channel.
connection.requestBodyDescription: JSON object passed to the method.
connection.securityDescription: Use SMTPS for port 465; STARTTLS for 25/587.
connection.passphraseDescription: Only when the key is encrypted.
connection.remotePathDescription: Optional path that must exist on the server.
connection.nodesDescription: Management API base URLs, one per line. UP when any node reports no alarms.
connection.closeCodesDescription: Close codes counted as UP, e.g. 1000.
connection.wsHeadersDescription: JSON object of extra handshake headers.
connection.ignoreAcceptHeaderDescription: Accept servers that answer without the header.
connection.gameDescription: GameDig game id, see <link>the games list</link>.
connection.givenPortOnlyDescription: Do not probe the other ports the game commonly uses.
connection.steam: The server is looked up through the Steam Web API. A superadmin must set the Steam API key in the instance settings first.
connection.remoteBrowserDescription: Playwright-compatible browser server (e.g. browserless or `npx playwright run-server`). Marmot does not launch Chromium itself.

http.title: HTTP options
http.description: Request shape and what counts as a healthy response.
http.headersDescription: JSON object of extra request headers.
http.proxyEmpty: No proxies yet; an admin can add one in <link>settings</link>.
http.proxyDescription: Send the request through an HTTP(s) or SOCKS proxy.
http.ignoreTlsDescription: Accept self-signed or expired certificates. Also disables certificate expiry notifications.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.upsideDownDescription: Flip the status: a failed check counts as UP and a successful one as DOWN.
advanced.certExpiryDescription: Warn through this monitor's notification channels before the TLS certificate expires (7, 14 and 21 days by default).
advanced.domainExpiryDescription: Look the registration up via RDAP once a day and warn before the domain expires.
advanced.activeDescription: Paused monitors keep their history but are not checked.

hero.title: Know it’s down before your users do.
hero.description: Marmot watches your websites, APIs and servers, alerts the right people the moment something breaks and keeps your customers informed with public status pages.

features.title: Everything Uptime Kuma does, built for a team
features.description: The monitors and notifications you already know, with organizations, roles and an API on top.

monitorTypes.title: 30+ monitor types
monitorTypes.body: HTTP and keywords, TCP, ping, DNS, Docker, databases, MQTT, gRPC, push heartbeats and more.

notifications.title: 40+ notification providers
notifications.body: Slack, Discord, Teams, email, ntfy, webhooks and the rest of the Uptime Kuma catalogue.

statusPages.title: Public status pages
statusPages.body: Branded pages on your own domain with incidents, RSS and per-group uptime.

maintenance.title: Maintenance windows
maintenance.body: Schedule one-off or recurring windows so planned work never pages anyone.

organizations.title: Organizations and roles
organizations.body: Invite your team, separate environments by organization and control who can change what.

live.title: Live by default
live.body: Heartbeats stream to the dashboard as they happen; no refresh button, no polling.

selfHost.title: Open source. Self-host it any time.
selfHost.description: Marmot is AGPL-3.0 software. Run the same image on your own server with Postgres or MongoDB and Redis, and keep every check and every heartbeat on infrastructure you control.
